dren-bio-2026.tagline: Clinical-stage biotech developing targeted antibody therapeutics for rare blood cancers.

founders.background: Serbian-born, Ph.D. from University of Belgrade, NIH postdoctoral researcher, former Vice President of Research at Allakos
founders.notable_achievement: Founded Dren Bio and raised $350M in investment; licensed platform technology to Sanofi.

product.summary: Dibotatug (DR-01) is the first antibody therapeutic targeting CD94, selectively eliminating pathogenic cytotoxic T cells to treat rare blood cancers while preserving the immune system.
product.problem_statement: Cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma (CTL) and large granular lymphocytic leukemia (LGLL) have no approved therapies and very poor prognoses.
product.solution: Dibotatug binds to CD94, selectively depleting pathogenic cells, and has demonstrated high response rates and safety in Phase 1/2 trials with over 300 patients dosed.
key_features: First-in-class CD94-targeted antibody
Preservation of immune system through selective pathogenic cell depletion
High complete response rate and safety in Phase 1/2 trials
Expanding indications beyond CTL and LGLL into aplastic anemia and autoimmune diseases
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Targeted Myeloid Engager and Phagocytosis Platform: A multispecific antibody technology targeting novel phagocytic receptors selectively expressed on myeloid cells. This platform can provide a safer therapeutic index than conventional T-cell engagers and ADCs.
product.target_customer: Patients with cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma, large granular lymphocytic leukemia, aplastic anemia, and autoimmune diseases.
product.business_model: In-house R&D and commercialization, or technology transfer and milestone revenue through partnerships with large pharmaceutical companies.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: First CD94-targeting antibody, selectively eliminates pathogenic cells for a safety advantage over existing immunotherapies. Unique mechanism of action utilizing phagocytic receptors.
competitive_landscape.moat: Proprietary Targeted Myeloid Engager and Phagocytosis Platform technology, validated by Sanofi's $600M upfront technology acquisition. Large investment raises financial strength.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Aiming for first approval in CTL and LGLL, with expectations of first-mover advantage given no currently approved therapies. Platform technology enables expansion into multiple indications.

trending_reason.summary: In October 2026, announced a massive $350M investment alongside preparation for dibotatug approval and commercialization plans. Positive Phase 1/2 data increases likelihood of approval.
catalysts: $350M oversubscribed investment round (October 2026)
Independent review of Phase 1/2 key data to be announced (December 2026)
Technology validation through Sanofi's acquisition of platform technology (2025)
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Over 300 patients dosed in Phase 1/2, high complete response and response rates (specific figures to be disclosed)

funding.total_raised_note: Series A $60M (2020), Series B $65M (2022), Series C $350M (2026). Some sources estimate total over $500M.

latest_round.note: Oversubscribed round; use of funds: late-stage clinical trials for dibotatug, regulatory submission, commercialization preparation. New investors: Juvia Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mirae Asset Capital Life Science, General Catalyst, Cormorant Asset Management, OrbiMed, among others.

product.summary: Reverion designs and manufactures reversible solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) power plants. product.problem_statement: The intermittency of solar and wind makes the grid unstable, and surging power demand from AI data centers outstrips grid expansion, creating an urgent need for stable, clean distributed power.
product.solution: Provides high-efficiency SOFC power plants that supply on-site 24/7 power and capture CO₂ to minimize environmental impact. Reversible electrolysis enables producing stored gas during power surplus, increasing grid flexibility.
key_features: Reversible operation: both power generation (SOFC) and electrolysis (SOEC) possible
World's highest electrical efficiency: 74.2% (field-proven), targeting 80%
Captures pure CO₂ during power generation, achieving carbon-negative operation
On-site installation and operation without distribution grid load; addresses data center power shortages

product.target_customer: Large-scale power consumers needing distributed power: biogas plants, AI data centers, hospitals, factories, etc.
product.business_model: Sells power plants (including maintenance) and is expanding a power purchase agreement (PPA) model. Cumulative project pipeline exceeds $2B.

Conventional gas turbines/engine generators (~40% efficiency). Large capacity but no carbon capture and grid-dependent.

competitive_landscape.moat: Patented process design and years of operational data; supply chain agreements with Doosan and others; secured 250MW production facility.

product.summary: Develops and supplies an all-optical integrated circuit switch module (OC-32M) and a silicon photonics-based switch chipset that accelerate data movement between GPUs inside AI data centers
product.problem_statement: As AI training/inference workloads scale to clusters of hundreds to thousands of GPUs, traditional electrical switches cause long latency and high power consumption due to optical transceiver conversion. Data movement speed is the core bottleneck for tokens per second per user performance
product.solution: On-chip optical circuit switching (OCS) technology that eliminates electrical-to-optical signal conversion. A two-chip design (switch chip + amplifier chip) compensates for optical loss, achieving ultra-low latency of ~10ns, ultra-low power under 1W/port, and a 200Gbit/s high-speed interface
key_features: Fully integrated silicon photonics-based all-optical switch (64-port demonstration completed, 128/256-port in development)
Port cost 1/10, power consumption under 1/8 compared to electrical switches
High-density configuration possible in 1U rack module form
Up to 52% improvement in tokens per second performance (initial simulation results)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Silicon photonics + proprietary optical amplification technology. Based on over 10 years of research from Oxford University and the University of Münster
product.target_customer: Hyperscalers, cloud providers, and large GPU farm operators that build/operate large-scale AI infrastructure
product.business_model: B2B sales of optical switch module and chipset hardware, with mass production through internal manufacturing partner Tower Semiconductor

direct_competitors.comparison: MEMS-based free-space optical OCS; Salience is not at a disadvantage in chip integration and power efficiency
Optical transceiver/switch business; Salience claims advantage in per-port cost and latency
Provides optical connectivity switches; Salience leads in silicon photonics integration density

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: The only 'on-chip (all-silicon photonic)' optical circuit switch. Competitors use MEMS or bulk optics, differentiated in integration density, mass production viability, and reliability
competitive_landscape.moat: Exclusive license to Oxford University and University of Münster research + two-chip optical amplification patent + strategic investment from AMD and Intel + preemptive mass production system through Tower Semiconductor foundry partnership
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: As the need for ultra-low-latency, low-power optical switches in AI infrastructure scale-up networks grows, Salience is the only one with a 'chip-level' OCS, positioning it to emerge as a key component in next-generation AI factories

founders.background: Research group leader, over 100 papers and multiple patents
founders.notable_achievement: Invented seRNA technology and fusogenic LNP delivery platform

srtd-biotech-2026.team_highlights: Matthias Alder (CEO): 30 years of biotech experience, held C-level positions at Autolus, GAIN Therapeutics, Novartis, etc., executed over $10B in transactions. Prof. Dr. Heinz Koeppl (CTO): Professor at TU Darmstadt, expert in synthetic biology and AI, over 170 papers. Dr. Jens Hennecke (CBO): Former executive at SOTIO and Micromet.

product.summary: The 'seRNA' platform that detects disease-specific RNA markers and expresses therapeutic proteins only in those cells. Drastically reduces systemic toxicity of conventional mRNA therapeutics.
product.problem_statement: Conventional mRNA therapeutics affect healthy cells as well, causing serious side effects and limiting the dosage that can be administered.
product.solution: In seRNA, the IRES blocker is removed only when a disease RNA marker is present inside the cell, activating the therapeutic effect. In healthy cells, it remains silent.
key_features: Dual selectivity: After delivery to the target organ via fusogenic LNP, seRNA detects the intracellular marker.
Modular design: The sensor and effector can be swapped to apply to various indications.
AI-based design: Discovery of RNA markers and structural optimization.
Fusogenic LNP: Enables delivery to various organs including the liver, lungs, and brain.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: seRNA (selective expression RNA) + fusogenic LNP (fusogenic lipid nanoparticles) + synthetic biology/AI platform
product.target_customer: Pharmaceutical companies developing therapeutics for hepatocellular carcinoma, lung cancer, liver fibrosis, and autoimmune diseases, or patients.
product.business_model: Develop pipeline internally, then submit IND and enter into licensing/partnership agreements.

direct_competitors.comparison: Leading mRNA companies, but lack cell-level switching technology like seRNA.
Strengths in personalized mRNA cancer vaccines, but cell-specific expression platform is at an early stage.
Systemic therapy based on self-replicating RNA, but cell selectivity is SRTD's proprietary technology.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: An on-off switch based on intracellular RNA markers to protect healthy cells.
competitive_landscape.moat: seRNA patents, fusogenic LNP technology, AI-based marker discovery pipeline.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The only platform that can overcome the safety limitations of mRNA therapeutics, securing a strong technological advantage at an early stage.

trending_reason.summary: Growing interest in the next-generation evolution of mRNA therapeutics after the success of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. Cell-specific expression is considered a key challenge in the mRNA field.
catalysts: €31.5 million seed investment raised on November 9, 2026
Strategic investment participation from big pharma including Boehringer Ingelheim

product.summary: The Mercury series is a diffusion-based large language model (dLLM) that delivers 5-10x faster speeds (up to 1,107 tokens/s) and 70% lower costs than traditional autoregressive LLMs
product.problem_statement: Existing LLMs suffer from high latency and cost due to the sequential token generation of autoregressive methods, and are less efficient in long-context or complex code tasks
product.solution: Applies diffusion models to language generation, generating multiple tokens in parallel to dramatically improve speed and efficiency. Fully supports existing LLM use cases like RAG, tool use, and agent workflows
key_features: First commercially viable dLLM (Mercury series)
1,107 tokens/s processing speed (Mercury 2.5)
4-8x faster than GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5
Low-latency real-time voice agent support (Mercury Voice)
Improved code generation, reasoning, and math problem-solving
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Discrete Diffusion Language Model (dLLM): Uses a diffusion process that generates the entire context simultaneously via a coarse-to-fine approach instead of autoregressive generation
product.target_customer: Fortune 500 companies, AI developers, companies building code editors and agent workflows, companies needing real-time voice interfaces
product.business_model: API-based usage billing (per token); enterprise licensing available

product.summary: Moonshot is an AI agent that continuously listens to a user's daily conversations through an iPhone app (Samantha) and a necklace-style wearable (Luna), and understands the context. It actively remembers promises, emotions, and plans, and proactively alerts users when needed.
product.problem_statement: Everyday conversations, promises, and emotions often go unrecorded and disappear. Existing digital tools only store and process information when users enter it manually.
product.solution: It listens to audio through the microphone on the app (or necklace), instantly transcribes and analyzes it into text, and builds a personal context database. Based on this, it reminds users of promises, tracks emotional trends, and connects with other AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT).
key_features: Ambient listening (mute with a double tap on the device)
Searchable transcripts of each day
Proactively remembers and reminds users of promises and plans they mention
Insights into emotions and life trends
Passes context to external AI such as Claude and ChatGPT
Automatic export to Google Docs
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Proprietary transcription service + LLM, privacy-first design (short-chunk transcription followed by deletion, permission-based data access)
product.target_customer: Individual users, early adopters of AI, busy modern professionals
product.business_model: App subscription ($25/month for the first year, then $50/month; additional $20/month for heavy usage); Luna hardware ($499 on Kickstarter), $1 deposit refundable

direct_competitors.comparison: Wearables that record and remember daily life; Moonshot focuses more on proactive recommendations.
